items.content:
Treasury announces bigger “debt buybacks.”

Bitcoin +12%. Gold +4%. US Dollar -1%.

Markets understand what this really means:
More deficits. More debt. And a desperate attempt at financial repression.

Instead of addressing the elephant in the room - higher interest rates driven by relentless spending and surging national debt - Treasury is resorting to financial shenanigans to suppress yields.Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello)The Treasury Department is calling this a “debt buyback.”

But they’re not reducing the debt.

They’re running huge deficits, buying back old bonds, and issuing even more new ones.

This is debt reshuffling, not debt reduction.—  https://x.com/charliebilello/status/2090074621865308482 
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Aug 20, 2026

items.title: RT by @charliebilello: RT by @charliebilello: The Fed is all talk and no action. Inflation isn’t cooling, yet markets don’t expect a rate hike in September. Further and further behind the curve they fall - and with every delay, their credibility as an inflation fighter erodes.
items.content:
The Fed is all talk and no action.

Inflation isn’t cooling, yet markets don’t expect a rate hike in September.

Further and further behind the curve they fall - and with every delay, their credibility as an inflation fighter erodes.Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello)The Fed spent years telling us 2% inflation was the goal.

But since January 2020, CPI has risen at a 4.0% annualized rate and is now 13% above a 2% inflation trend.

That’s not "price stability." It’s a massive failure of monetary policy.—  https://x.com/charliebilello/status/2087530980194050463
